1. VWAP in plain words

  • VWAP (volume-weighted average price) = the average price of the day, where prices with more volume count more. It is roughly "the average price everyone paid today". VWAP = Σ(price × volume) ÷ Σ volume, added up from the start of the session (or another anchor).
  • Price can be the typical price (H+L+C)/3 (TradingView default), the close, or (O+H+L+C)/4.
  • Above VWAP: buyers are paying more than the day's average → buyers in control (long bias). Below VWAP: sellers in control (short bias). A cross of VWAP = control may be changing.
  • Why it matters: big funds judge their fills against VWAP (buying below it = a good fill), so the line attracts orders and often acts as moving support/resistance.
  • The VWAP moves faster when price is far from it and volume is high; quiet low-volume bars barely move it.
  • It resets every session, which is why the line jumps at each day's open.

2. Bands, anchors, settings

  • Bands = standard deviations around VWAP: band k = VWAP ± k × σ, σ = volume-weighted std of price from the anchor. Roughly 68% / 95% / 99% of trading sits inside band 1 / 2 / 3 (only if prices were normally distributed — they aren't). Band 1 = normal pullbacks; bands 2–3 = stretched / extreme prices.
  • Anchor = where the VWAP starts adding up. Session (day trading), week (1-hour charts), month (4-hour / daily), quarter, earnings date, or any candle you pick (anchored VWAP from a major high/low or news candle).
  • Rolling VWAP = never resets; uses a fixed look-back window instead.

3. The VWAP course's trading rules

  1. Biggest mistake: buying just because price touched VWAP. VWAP is context, not a trigger. A flat VWAP (sideways market) gives the most false signals.
  2. Method A — mean reversion: VWAP flat, price stretches to band 1–2, a reversal candle forms → trade back to VWAP.
  3. Method B — trend continuation: VWAP clearly sloping, price pulls back to VWAP (or band 1), a hammer/engulfing forms → trade with the trend.
  4. Final strategy (reversal): all three must line up — touch of band 2 + an old horizontal support/resistance level (best with a failure test: a quick break of the level that closes back) + a candle pattern (shooting star, hammer, engulfing, morning/evening star). Enter at the candle close, stop just past the pattern's extreme, target 2R.

4. Volume profile and the POC (video 2)

  • Volume profile = a sideways histogram of how much volume traded at each price over a range (not per time bar).
  • POC (point of control) = the price with the most volume. High-volume areas act like resistance (price struggles through them); low-volume areas let price move fast.
  • Currency Pros use it as a bonus check on their own checklist (4 × 25 points): higher-timeframe alignment (sell when the daily chart is in the top half of its range, buy in the bottom half), break of structure, liquidity sweep (a false break of an old high/low), imbalance (fair-value gap). They enter with limit orders at the 67% (≈1:2) or 75% (≈1:3) Fibonacci retracement of the range, stop beyond the range, target the other end.
  • POC rule: POC at your entry level = stronger setup. POC at the far end of the range, next to your stop = skip it — price tends to get pulled there and hit the stop.
  • On stocks the volume is real exchange volume; in forex/CFDs it is only your broker's volume.

5. What my backtests showed (Nifty 50 + Nifty 200, FYERS costs)

ApproachResult
VWAP course, every setup, 1-min → dailyNot worth trading. Raw band touches: median win rate 27%. Each added check (candle, level) helped, but the median Sharpe stayed negative; intraday win rates 28–47% vs 41–60% needed after charges
VWAP swing (weekly / monthly anchor), deliveryLost in most settings; best 6–9% a year, below just holding the stocks (14–19%)
Currency Pros + POC, 5-min / 1-hour / 4-hourLost on both stock lists
Currency Pros + POC, 15-min intraday, full checklistLead: Nifty 200 all 7 settings profitable, best +₹1.35L on ₹10L in 11 months, 51% wins vs 40% needed — but mostly in Jun–Oct 2026; only 2 of 7 settings positive in both halves. Nifty 50: roughly flat (−₹22k to +₹15k)
Currency Pros + POC, daily deliveryNifty 200: 4–11% a year in 2022–26, beat random entries — but below holding the stocks (18.9%). Nifty 50: 1–4% a year
The POC filter itselfLittle help. "Skip if POC near stop": no change on average. "POC at entry": helped intraday (17 of 24 pairs), not delivery
The full checklist (sweep + higher-TF)Helped clearly: better in 26 of 36 pairs, intraday and delivery

6. Takeaways

  • The course's warning is correct: VWAP alone is not an edge. Extra confirmation helps, but not enough to pay intraday costs.
  • In the Currency Pros setup, the checklist did the work, not the volume profile.
  • Only lead worth paper trading: 15-min, full checklist, 75% limit entry, intraday, on liquid stocks — compare live results with the backtest for 3+ months before risking money.
  • Videos show the clearest examples, picked by eye. Fixed rules on 50–200 stocks are a much harder test.
